A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LUSD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material support comparison, including matching content across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MagicBrush evaluations, human preference results, ablations, and qualitative experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds moving-average ablation results, a controlled metric-bias experiment, runtime measurements, and additional SBP comparisons.

M1.justification: The SBP-based optimization, attention masks, moving average, spatial regularization, gradient filtering, and normalization remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 retain the same procedure; the new moving-average study evaluates an existing component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover MagicBrush object insertion and general editing, alongside in-the-wild images. The new ablation and location-bias diagnostic investigate retained editing coverage; their subset selection and placement controls change experimental design rather than introducing a new domain or task.

E2.justification: SBP, already evaluated in v1's Table 2 and Figure 8, is added to the human comparison in Table 1, the object-insertion comparison in Table 3, and Figure 7. Paint-by-Example generates diagnostic examples rather than serving as a new competitor against LUSD.

E3.justification: v2 adds a moving-average on/off control and a 70-case diagnostic comparing same-sized, nonoverlapping insertion regions using Paint-by-Example. Table 2 also adds runtime reporting. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; the added SBP human comparison is not reconciled with the appendix's five-competitor protocol.

E4.justification: New Appendix 7, Figure 11, and Table 5 isolate attention-mask localization and moving averaging. Appendix 9.3 and Table 7 experimentally test whether reference-based metrics penalize alternative insertion locations. These extend v1's existing component ablations and metric-bias analysis.

E5.justification: New Table 7 reports p-values of 2.33e-9, 1.88e-2, and 1.28e-3 for the 70-case location-bias experiment. v1 has no corresponding significance analysis. The test type is unspecified, and existing seed demonstrations and human-vote aggregation remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing aggregate benchmark scores are retained. v2 adds SBP insertion scores, runtime entries, qualitative outputs, and results in Tables 5 and 7. New Table 1 reports SBP preferred over LUSD 57.7% overall under its caption, contradicting the retained claim that LUSD wins every comparison; v1 had no SBP human-preference row.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, attention-mask updates, normalization, metric definitions, and DDS extension remain unchanged. The new diagnostic supplies empirical evidence rather than a new theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about reliable editing, object insertion, background preservation, and shared hyperparameters. Added evidence does not revise these claims, including the preference claim now inconsistent with the SBP row.

C2.justification: New Appendix 7 clarifies that attention masks localize updates even without moving averaging, distinguishing localization from averaging's additional benefit. Existing explanations of metric bias, unnatural placement, slow filtering, and limited language understanding are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: Table 2 newly discloses editing times, including 1.79 minutes for LUSD. Appendix 9.3 documents pixel-difference region extraction, Unsplash object exemplars, and placement controls. Existing implementation details remain unchanged; hardware and timing conditions are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds the EditVal reference and relates its human-evaluation criteria to that work. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged; most citation-number changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 adds a moving-average appendix section, expands the metric-bias passage, and makes localized wording edits. It introduces the IP2P abbreviation, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgements. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 7 gains an SBP row and another example, but its final two prompt labels are mismatched. v2 also adds Figure 11 and Tables 5 and 7, expands existing tables, revises Figure 8's labels and caption, and reflows appendix material.

improvement.justification: The added ablation, controlled metric-bias test, and runtime disclosure strengthen validation and transparency. However, the new SBP preference results contradict the retained superiority claim, while Appendix 9.2 still describes only five competitors; Figure 7 also introduces mislabeled examples. These reporting problems affect central evidence, and the PDFs do not resolve the SBP discrepancy sufficiently to judge a reliable net improvement.
